findings.claim: ADR 0029's change is a bullet appended inside Consequences, but okf-bundle.md says a record is never rewritten and a correction is an appended '## Correction, YYYY-MM-DD' section (as in ADR 0006, 0011, 0019). The Decision section still says 'A priority-0 global rule' with nothing next to it pointing at the correction.
Two concepts were edited by hand (components/bifrost, decisions/0029) but no line naming them was appended to .okf/log.md, which the every-touched-concept-is-logged constraint requires.

Two edited lines run past 80 columns. The bifrost.md line ending 'A timeout or classifier error leaves the requested model' and the services.tf comment line ending 'Alphabetical by `provider` -- see' were not rewrapped after the edit.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
bifrost.hcl moves the four routing rules to 10 to 13 with the passthrough first.
The test now enforces unique priorities, all above 3, with the passthrough first.
The services.tf comment sits outside any heredoc or jobspec.
Apart from the ADR's original Decision text, nothing in the repo still says the passthrough is at priority 0.
The gates are green.
The remaining findings are about the knowledge bundle's own rules (correction format, log line) plus line wrapping.
None of them blocks.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: pass pre_commit, pass cli_tests, pass r1, pass r2, stamp green f940c72a7a56f087207ee145c9d7b87b40a4bcc951b965ca33fab600d8d6caa7.
`uv run --directory cli pytest tests/test_bifrost_router.py -q`: 9 passed.
`kmctl check`: all checks passed.

r1: test_complexity_router sorts by priority and asserts the set size equals the list length (catches a shared priority), checks `min > 3` (catches any rule at 3 or below), and requires the lowest one to carry the passthrough CEL and the weight-only target (catches the passthrough not being first).
Each part of fails_when is asserted.
Setting the old 0 to 3 back would fail on min.
r3 (judgment): this cannot be checked until the operator applies.
The reasoning holds.
Bifrost stops at the first matching rule.
The hand-made rules at 0 to 3 run first and never name complexity_tier, so Claude Code requests keep their aliases and pay no classifier call.
Router-key requests that miss those rules then reach 10 to 13 as before.
The implementer's local 2.3.1 reproduction (old config fatal, new config boots with eight rules) fits the error the plan quotes.
r3 stays open for the operator's apply and the smoke run.
Grepped the repo outside .git and .loop for priority 0 claims.
The only one left is ADR 0029's Decision text, covered by f1.
f1: Turn the Consequences bullet into a `## Correction, 2026-11-16` section at the end of ADR 0029, following ADR 0006, 0011 and 0019.
Do not edit the Decision text.
Amending this ADR, not writing a new one, is the right call: it fixes a fact (the priority numbers) and does not reverse the choice.
f2: Append a 2026-11-16 line to `.okf/log.md` naming `components/bifrost` and `decisions/0029-bifrost-routes-by-complexity-for-one-virtual-key-and-adds-jev`, with the reason.
f3: Rewrap the two long lines.
